tasks.title: Verify the vault-isolation leak stays closed
tasks.note: **FIXED and SHIPPED as v0.22.1 (`e633fcb`, diagnosed by Atlas, committed by Forge, Session 53). The guard caught its own committer on day one.** The test suite had been writing session summaries into Aaron's **real** Obsidian vault: 13 files named `2026-08-31-ob-server-{slug}.md`, 69 bytes each, frontmatter `project: ob-server-Cz4UxZ` with an empty `sessionId` and a body of `test`. Found at `/end` while listing `Summaries/`. **This is a recurrence with the guard already in place** — `tests/setup-env.ts` has set `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` to a temp vault since the 57-file incident in April, and `vitest.config.ts` loads it. **Root cause — CORRECTED after shipping; the first diagnosis named a real hazard but not the producer.** The demonstrated producer is **`npx vitest` run from the REPO ROOT**: there is no `vitest.config.*` above `open-brain/`, so a root-level run discovers the tests by default glob and loads **no config at all** — `setupFiles` never executes, `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` is never set, and the whole suite runs unisolated against the real vault. Forge's cwd had drifted to the repo root mid-session (a mirror-copy `cd`), so its full-suite runs today wrote the 13 files. Proven twice over: from the root the new guard produced **23 failures**; from `open-brain/`, 688/688 and zero new artifacts. *(Atlas's original diagnosis — `index-v2.test.ts:55`, `skill-scan-runner.test.ts:33`, `apoptosis-reachability.test.ts:138` each `delete` the variable in `afterEach` rather than restoring it, so within a reused worker every later test falls through `paths.ts` to `join(homedir(), …)` — is a **real second path to the same leak** and is also closed by the fix, but it was never shown to have produced a file. Recorded rather than deleted: two independent routes to one silent failure is the point, not a tally of who was right.)* `server.test.ts:16` is the writer in both routes — it runs session-end against `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "ob-server-"))` and `writeSummary` deposits a summary named for the temp project. **Same invariant as the day's other four instances:** an unset `OPEN_BRAIN_VAULT_DIR` *means* "use production", so absent and configured are the same value from inside the resolver and the guard's own removal is unobservable. **Fix, two parts:** (1) `setup-env.ts` re-asserts the override in a global `afterEach`, so no teardown can leave a worker unprotected whatever it does to the variable; (2) `obsidianVaultDir()` throws when running under vitest and the path resolves to the *real* home vault — a synthetic home is still allowed, so `paths.test.ts`'s deliberate fallback assertion is untouched. Structural prevention plus a loud failure, per the v0.15.1 precedent that removing a read is not the same as counting what you no longer read. **Evidence it holds:** typecheck clean, **688 tests / 49 files green** (+1 = the new test pinning the leak), and a full suite run produced **zero** new `ob-server` files. The 13 artifacts were deleted (Aaron approved); 154 legitimate summaries remain. **What is owed next session:** confirm zero `ob-server-*` in `~/Obsidian Vault v2/Summaries/` after a fresh full run from `open-brain/`. **Revised on the /sync question** — the earlier "no check needed" was wrong, because it assumed the throw always runs, and the root-run route is precisely the case where it does not (no config, no setup, and until v0.22.1 no failure either). Two follow-ups, both filed separately: a `/sync` counter for `ob-server-*` in the vault (there is a preventer and still **no detector** — this was found by accident while listing `Summaries/` at `/end`, not by any check), and a root-level vitest config-or-refuse so a root run fails as one clear message instead of 23 scattered ones. **Also noticed, not fixed:** the artifact filenames lowercase (`ob-server-cz4uxz.md`) while the frontmatter preserves case (`ob-server-Cz4UxZ`) — invisible on Windows, two identities on Linux/macOS, the same blind spot already filed against `ob_store` deriving vault folder names from a canonicalized path. (Session 53)

tasks.title: `ob_store` derives the vault folder from a canonicalized path, so it lowercases the project name
tasks.note: (Session 49). `server.ts:537` computes `projectName = effectiveProject.split("/").pop()` from the *canonical* `project_dir`, and `canonicalizeProjectDir` lowercases the **entire string** when it starts with a drive letter — not just the drive. Result: `ob_store` writes `Experiences/self-improving-agent/` while the `store()` pipeline given an explicit project name writes `Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/`. **Two live rows already differ** — #235 (older) and #365 (stored during this close-out). **Invisible on Windows** because the filesystem is case-insensitive, so both resolve into the one real folder, `checkVaultIndexParity` passes, and nothing dangles. On macOS or Linux this silently creates a **second project folder**, which `skill-scan` reads as a separate project and which reproduces the exact 60-duplicate divergence repaired earlier this same session. The general rule it violates: **a canonical form is for comparison, not for display** — deriving a human-facing name from a lossy identity key reuses a transformation for a purpose it was not built for. Fix: carry the display name separately (the caller already knows it) rather than reconstructing it from the key; then repoint the two existing rows. Related to the P3 cross-platform item — this is a second Windows-only blind spot. Now documented as §10 of the `path-normalization` skill.

Then document live `SendMessage` as primary with the mailbox as the fallback for a peer that isn't running, state the durable contract (*if it must survive the session it is a decision or a task, written in that form*), and move the five dead channels under `archive/`. **Stageable today with no code change** — a blank `mailbox_channel` already skips the surface (`AGENT.md:21`); the code change only sets the default. tasks.title: Give each agent seat its own git worktree
tasks.note: Session 62: two seats share one working tree at C:/Users/melve/Projects/Self-Improving-Agent (git worktree list returns exactly one entry). The Planner branched off master without checking which branch the tree was on, committed 19 newly-tracked instruction files, and opened PR #17. Switching to that branch and back DELETED 19 files from disk - all of .claude/commands/, CLAUDE.md, .agents/AGENT.md, LIFECYCLE.md, the four SYSTEM/ files, domains.json and the skills - because they are tracked on the new branch and absent from loop/11-instructions, so git checkout removed them. They were backed up first and all 19 restored; the Developer's uncommitted C3 work survived as pure additions (verified: 173 insertions, 0 deletions, on top of ddba9d0). NOBODY DID ANYTHING WRONG ON THEIR OWN BRANCH - that is the point. Either seat can delete the other's files by performing a correct operation, nothing warns either party, and the loss is silent for untracked files because git does not report removing what it never tracked. Same shape as the read-ordering watch-out: within one seat you can order your actions; across two seats neither party controls the tree. Fix: one worktree per seat off the same repository (git worktree add ../sia-planner <branch>), so branches cannot collide in a shared checkout. Evidence: this incident, Planner error 30, session 62. Filing this task evicted done-task T-004 under retention (G-024); its content is preserved in CHANGELOG.md under Loop 11.

tasks.title: An unrecognised CLI flag must refuse, not select the mutating default
tasks.note: Session 62: `node open-brain/build/cli.js sync --check-only` was run intending a dry run. There is no such flag. cli.ts:21 is `args.includes("--check")` — exact array membership, so "--check-only" does not match, checkOnly stayed false, the flag was SILENTLY DISCARDED and sync ran in FIX MODE, writing seven tracked files plus untracked PRD.md. No harm that time only because every write was version-sync the release bump required anyway, and the diff was read before committing — WHICH MEANS THE SAFETY CAME FROM THE OPERATOR, NOT THE TOOL. Loop 11's other 38 defects were prose that lied about behaviour; this is behaviour that lies about intent, and it is the more dangerous class: a mistyped safety flag selects the unsafe path and says nothing. Fix: parse argv against a known flag set and exit non-zero on anything unrecognised, naming the flag. Deterministic, and it cannot be overridden the way a documented convention can. Applies to every subcommand of cli.ts, not just sync. Evidence: cli.ts:21, and the seven-file write at 811dddc's parent.

tasks.title: The test suite is not type-checked at all
tasks.note: open-brain/tsconfig.json is `"include": ["src/**/*"]` and there is exactly one tsconfig, so `tsc` NEVER READS open-brain/tests/. Not 'checked less strictly' — not checked. Found in Loop 12 R-010: cutting `enableHeuristicRatings` left the flag named in six places across four test files and `npx tsc --noEmit` exited 0. The referrers surfaced only at runtime, when assertions happened to trip on them. This reframes '603 tests passing': the suite proves behaviour, and nothing proves the tests' own types. A type error in a test is invisible unless a runtime assertion happens to catch it. Fix is a tsconfig that includes tests (or a second one for typecheck only); the risk is that it surfaces a backlog of existing test type errors, which is the point. Independent of the retirement work — filed, not fixed, in the loop that found it.

tasks.title: Shadow merge gate: the runtime records what it would have done at each merge, and disagreements with Aaron are counted
tasks.note: DERIVED FROM THE AUTONOMY RULING (see the decision recorded this revision). At every point where a merge to master could occur, the runtime writes a would-merge / would-not-merge verdict with its reasons — deterministic check results, QA E_t status, and once the gates exist, their typed answers — into artifacts/iterations/tNNN/. Aaron still merges. The runtime then records his actual decision beside its own, and the count of disagreements is the instrument that decides when the human gate is removed. BELONGS TO SLICE TWO OR LATER, not Loop 15: it needs the gates to have an opinion, and it needs the merge point to exist in the runtime first. NOT RULED AS THE NEXT LOOP'S SUBJECT. Design constraints that come from the record: the verdict must be written BEFORE Aaron decides, so it cannot be fitted to his answer; both verdicts carry the candidate SHA and a timestamp; a run where the runtime could not form a verdict (gate unreachable, evidence missing) is recorded as UNDEFINED and never as agreement. Zero disagreements across loops with NO real defects in the stream is not evidence of anything — the count only means something when the loops contained failures a gate could have caught.

tasks.title: /start must assert a transcript exists for the session's own uuid — the CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION check would be a permanent false positive
tasks.note: REWRITTEN session 77 after the recorded cause was falsified. The rev-62 note said all three Loop 16 seats (planner 22631f4e, developer 46758737, QA 6eab2c5c) wrote no .jsonl because they carried CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 inherited from the VS Code window. tasks.title: Close-outs must APPEND a per-seat record, not overwrite a shared slot — plus a /sync check that no close-out reduces the recorded seat-uuid count for an open loop
tasks.note: Opened session 77 from the Loop 16 correction. Measured: rev 61's QA close-out removed the developer's uuid (1 -> 0) and added its own (0 -> 2) in the same commit; rev 62 did the same in the other direction. The slot therefore only ever holds the last seat to close, and every loop whose seats close in sequence loses all but one seat's evidence with nothing noticing. This is why the developer's uuid was missing from the QA seat's tree a day later and why a correctly-run grep there returned a true zero that read as absence. DETERMINISTIC FIX (Aaron's stated preference over prompt-level guidance): make the slot a list keyed by seat so a close-out can only append its own entry. CHECK SHAPE, proposed by the developer seat and attributed to it: 'no close-out removes a uuid another seat's close-out added', cheap to implement against the rendered views. A /sync assertion turns a silent overwrite into a failed check. Not add_gap: R28 holds until T-158 lands.

tasks.title: Evaluate an alternate harness/model as the DEVELOPER seat via T-155's shadow merge gate — Aaron's named candidate is DeepSeek v4.1 Flash
tasks.note: Opened session 77 at Aaron's request; the driver is usage cost, not capability doubt. DECIDE IT BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT: run the alternate harness as a SHADOW developer on the same brief and the same base SHA as the real developer seat, record what it would have done at each merge, and count disagreements — the instrument is T-155's shadow merge gate, so this task is BLOCKED until T-155 lands in Loop 15 slice three. Report disagreement count and kind, not a verdict on the model. WHY THE DEVELOPER SEAT AND NOT THE OTHERS: the developer is the only seat whose output is checked by something that is not the developer — V-038 (write allowlist reverts an out-of-band write), V-039 (refuses a moved or dirty tree against the candidate SHA), V-040 (exhausted retry cap is a recorded failure), V-041 (verdicts from exit codes alone), V-044 (sees committed changes, not only the working tree). A weaker developer yields worse code, not a false record. QA is the opposite — QA IS the check and nothing sits behind it: session 77's evidence is the QA seat refusing success:true as proof of delivery, demanding a citation for a uuid mapping three agents had relayed unlabelled, and catching a mangled-ref false zero only because it carried a known-present control. None of that is mechanically enforceable. The planner is worse still: it writes criteria before any candidate exists and nothing downstream checks the criteria. So the swap candidate is the developer seat only. KNOWN BLOCKERS FOR A CURSOR-HOSTED SEAT, already recorded: G-001 (Cursor start.md/end.md copies are not on ob_start/ob_state), G-009 (the template's Cursor start.md still writes .recalled-entries.json, so R4 is Claude-only), T-046 (Cursor + Git Bash: the PowerShell hook wrapper fail-closes EVERY tool — broken, not degraded). COST THAT PARTLY CANCELS THE SAVING: D-029 makes native cross-session messaging the transport for seats on one machine; a non-Claude-Code seat cannot use it and returns to the A2A hub for that edge, so hub operating cost is traded for model cost. CHEAPER LEVER, MEASURE IT FIRST: session 77 spent a long three-seat exchange on a transport investigation that a two-seat exchange would have mostly produced. How often three seats are convened is a larger lever than which model sits in them, and it costs nothing to try.

decisions.title: Amendment vocabulary: which state records can be corrected, and which are append-only
decisions.note:
Decided once rather than one op per incident. The op union grew by accident — update_task exists because someone needed it, update_gap did not because nobody had yet — and Loop 5 hit the consequence twice in one night.

RULE: a record is amendable when its text DESCRIBES SOMETHING STILL BEING LEARNED. A record is append-only when its text IS THE HISTORICAL FACT, so that editing it destroys the thing the record exists to preserve.

Per type:
- TASKS — amendable (open/update/close/reopen). Title and priority are current intent, which legitimately changes. Already correct.
- GAPS — amendable. A gap describes something we do not yet understand, so its text is provisional by construction. The record most needing correction was the one that could not be corrected. IMPLEMENTED this loop: update_gap. The prior workaround (close + re-add) silently minted a new id and reset opened_session, losing the history the gap list exists to keep.
- VERIFIED — claim append-only; evidence appends; status reopens. The claim is what evidence was gathered against, so editing it invalidates that evidence silently while leaving it attached. Already correct; no update_verified.
- DECISIONS — append-only. A decision log records what was decided and when; amending it is not a correction but a rewrite of the record. Supersede with a new decision instead. Already correct; no update_decision. Gap: decisions carry no supersedes field (tasks do), so superseding is convention only.
- OBJECTIVE / HANDOFF / LAST_SESSION — singletons, set wholesale. Already correct.
- PROJECT.VERSION — REMOVE; do not add set_version. No consumer treats it as authoritative: cli.ts:427 and session-start/state-render.ts:14 display it, state-import/index.ts:439,494 copy it, drift-detector.ts:9 + checks-state.ts:73 + checks.ts:783 compare it to package.json and complain, and state-writer.ts:166 prefers package.json with this only as fallback. It is a cached copy of a truth held elsewhere, with a drift branch and two checks existing solely to police the cache. DEFERRED to Loop 7: 7 call sites plus schema, a state.json migration and test updates is larger than the decision.

ID SCHEME, observed while filing this: the Planner's brief assumed the next ADR id was free, but ADR-021..ADR-026 already exist and nextId has since minted D-001..D-003 alongside them, so the list now carries both schemes. This decision took an explicit ADR-027 to avoid widening the split. The generation bug itself stays filed under G-005 — it is an id question, not an amendment one.

Reasoning: recency_strong tests ONE alternative point against ONE incumbent. That 0.02 beats 0.005 is evidence the constant is too low. It is not evidence that 0.02 is right — nothing between or beyond was measured, and the optimum could be anywhere above 0.005. Adopting the one other number that happened to be guessed in the strategy list is the 'flipped because the new number is bigger' outcome the loop's own precondition rules out, and it rules it out whether or not the bigger number won.

shadow/index.ts states the same contract independently: changing production constants stays a human decision; the harness only supplies the evidence. The evidence is now worth supplying, which it was not before this loop.

decisions.title: ADR-029 - Keep session-start retrieval; suspend the maturity lifecycle; leave the causal question unasked
decisions.note: Loop 7's deliverable, RECOMMENDED not yet adopted - Aaron rules (T-129). 'Does injection earn its place' was three questions wearing one coat, and bundling them is what nearly retired the cheap half on evidence that only ever concerned the expensive half. STEM Agent's argument is that a maturation lifecycle belongs on an EXECUTABLE unit because only an execution yields an objective outcome; that indicts success_rate, maturity and apoptosis on knowledge entries and says nothing about whether fetching a note is worthwhile. A bookmark is not improved by a promotion ladder. Keep retrieval: the case against it was a claim retracted in the vault 26 minutes after it was written, and the first adequately powered contrast this project has produced runs in its favour (start 0.337 vs explicit 0.259 per-entry, n=109 and n=56, opposite to the pre-registration's own selection-bias prediction). Per prereg §5 that is not evidence injection helps - it refutes the claim that injection is the low-value mode. Suspend the lifecycle: success_rate is near-two-valued (98% of rated entries read exactly 1.0), apoptosis cannot fire on arithmetic (needs >=4 harmful on one entry, observed max 1), no_maturity tied live in Loop 6, and the ladder is a ratchet. Recency decay by contrast IS validated, so this is not 'ranking is worthless'. The causal question: control arm named concretely (randomised withhold flag in sessions at ob_start plus a non-self-reported outcome) and then argued against on the pre-registration's own costing - at ~2 sessions/week no effect smaller than enormous is resolvable.

Rows produced after the fix are out of sample for Loop 7, the population having been fixed before the change. Secondary rule, and the part that was nearly missed: with the gate closed an unjudged entry is SKIPPED, not recorded neutral - a fallback neutral is indistinguishable from a rater's considered 'retrieved and not used', so the cheaper diff would have destroyed the only signal the corpus still has while appearing to strengthen the data.

decisions.title: ADR-031 - a sign-off transfers across an amend only when the amend is provably disjoint

Paired with the error-table admission rule: the table records a wrong claim that reached an artifact, a commit, a counterpart or Aaron; a near-miss caught in-process by its own author goes in a separate register as an instance of a named family, never numbered. THE DIVIDING LINE IS ESCAPE, NOT SEVERITY. Both rules exist to stop a correctness rule taxing the behaviour it wants - a rule that adds a row every time someone checks their own work makes checking your own work look like failure. decisions.title: The HoH loop is autonomous inside a branch; Aaron holds master until the shadow-gate count says otherwise
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat, by returning the planner's recommendation verbatim: 'autonomous inside a branch, you at master, with the runtime recording what it would have done at each merge so your disagreements become a count. The day that count is zero across loops with real defects in them, remove the gate on evidence.' THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT RECORDED IN docs/HOH-JEV.md §6.2 AND docs/loops/loop-15-brief.md §5.1: hoh_jev.md specified a loop that never blocks on a human, which was incompatible with 'Aaron merges, on his word', a rule that has held for every loop in this record. WHAT IS AUTONOMOUS: the plan gate, the developer done-gate, QA scoring, retry, and rollback — closed questions with criteria written in advance, run by the runtime without a human. WHAT IS NOT: the merge to master. The runtime stops at a candidate commit and never merges, pushes to master, or tags. WHY THE MERGE STAYS HUMAN, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN NERVES: every serious defect found recently passed the automated checks and was caught by a human question or a human-ordered real run — the retirements check green through five merged PRs then 115 findings in the main tree; build-freshness shipped with its author's tests green and wrong in two checkouts of three; the main tree fifteen commits stale and reporting pass. A gate is a calibrated judge of the evidence it is shown, and every one of those failures was in the evidence, not the judgement. TypeSafe's own words: typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. THE EXIT CRITERION IS MEASURABLE: the runtime records, at every merge decision, what it WOULD have done. Aaron still merges. Each time his decision differs from the runtime's is counted. When that count is zero across several loops that contained real defects, the human gate is redundant and is removed — on evidence. If it is not zero, the count is exactly what would have been lost. This is 'see it red before you trust it green' applied to the human gate itself. WHAT NO GATE REPLACES, stated so it is not quietly automated later: asking the question nobody wrote down. Jev answers questions it is asked; the observation that Loop 14 was briefed against a world that no longer existed came from a person noticing, not from a gate.

The two rules JSON Schema cannot express — new_capability non-empty unless stop_ship is requested and justified, repair_targets non-empty — are written into the generated files' own description, so a reader validating against the file alone is told what it cannot see. Regenerate with `npx tsx src/harness/cli.ts schemas --write`; it refuses to write into a build directory.

decisions.note: AMENDS D-028, whose premise was that Claude Code cross-session discovery is broken on this machine. That premise is FALSE and was tested end to end on 2026-09-21 with three live seats (planner sia-planner-1c, developer sia-forge-42, QA sia-qa-24). All six directions were attested BY THE RECEIVING SIDE, never by a send receipt: both seats independently refused to treat success:true as delivery. An idle seat wakes on inbound with no human in the path — measured at 1.486s from receipt to first tool call. The queue-hold hypothesis is excluded by MAGNITUDE (|delta| = 227ms between the sender's success return and the receiver's context receipt, against the seconds-to-minutes a human-gated hold predicts), which does not require trusting two processes' log clocks at sub-second resolution; the ordering (delivery BEFORE the sender's own acknowledgment) is suggestive but not load-bearing. D-028's hub deployment keeps its role for CROSS-MACHINE traffic and for the Grok bot; it is no longer the default for seats on one box. Known limit, from the QA seat: ListAgents has a registration lag — the developer's listing showed only the planner while the QA seat was already running, and an early or short listing is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a seat that is not running. Nothing may gate on a single ListAgents poll.

ob_stats SHOWING `hook: 1` IS NOT EVIDENCE THE SERVER KNOWS ABOUT THE TRIGGER. That census is a GROUP BY over recall_log values, so a stale build prints it from data alone. A QUOTING LAYER BETWEEN YOU AND THE ARTIFACT EDITS THE CONTENT AND REPORTS SUCCESS. Four instances this session: a heredoc'd backslash became a real newline inside a TypeScript string literal (syntax-broken mutant, all twelve tests red, looks exactly like the result you wanted); a heredoc'd regex never compiled so a fixture was never modified and the test passed against it — which read as A FALSE ACCUSATION against a working guard; a backticked word in a hub message was executed as a command substitution and the clause arrived missing its subject; and json.dumps without ensure_ascii=False escaped every em-dash in Aaron's settings.json. WRITE EVERY SCRIPT AND EVERY MESSAGE TO A FILE, including one-liners, and have mutation scripts ASSERT THE EDIT LANDED before running anything.

tsc --noEmit ON EVERY MUTANT, BEFORE COUNTING IT. Three mutants this session were type-invalid and proved nothing while looking red or green as convenient — TS2349 from calling an object instead of its method, and an invented field that fell back to the real one at run time. A mutant that breaks syntax or types is not a mutant.

A FIXTURE CAN FAIL IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION, and that is harder to see than a vacuous one because it looks like rigour. My first A1 decoy carried all three query terms in one short sentence and beat entry 299; the developer's rank-9 fixture gave every decoy a length advantage. Both exaggerated the defect. Measure your fixture's shape — decoy lengths against the target's — and report the range.

THE DERIVATION READS ELEMENTS, NOT WORDS. `zzqqxxyy 2>&1 | tail -3; echo $?` derives all three terms and injects, because the recogniser sees a trimmer pipeline and a $? read. You cannot produce a SILENT fire with nonsense command text; use a three-document store, where bm25's IDF collapses and nothing clears the floor.

EVERY ROW YOU RUN, RUNS ON THIS MACHINE. CI is the second machine and it found two faults in one file the first time it looked, both of which passed every local run including three full suites. Cite a CI run id as evidence, and treat an empty statusCheckRollup as PRE-REGISTRATION and not a pass — mine was genuinely empty for ~3.5 minutes after the push before the run appeared.

NOTHING IS PUSHED FROM THIS SEAT. The planner pushes QA branches by the SHA this seat reports, on Aaron's word for that push. Every push names a BRANCH TIP, never an interior commit — a report correction is auditable only if the thing it corrects travels with it.

REGISTERING THE HOOK IN ~/.claude/settings.json IS MACHINE-WIDE, not QA-tree-wide: two of the ten fire rows from the A7 probe carry other seats' session uuids. A mutant found it; no amount of reading would have. When a test asserts on a value, check the instrument actually carries that value to the assertion.

A THRESHOLD COMPARED AGAINST bm25 IS CORPUS-RELATIVE, AND A FIXTURE THAT DOES NOT RESEMBLE THE CORPUS CANNOT TEST IT. The same query scores about 5e-6 against three documents and 14.01 against 599. At the shipped floor a small store is silent for EVERY input, so 'the floor silenced the weak match' passes with the floor doing no work at all. floor.test.ts carries a row asserting its own corpus is still at production scale; if that row ever goes red, every floor assertion under it has gone vacuous rather than wrong.

A STACKED FIXTURE PROVES AS LITTLE AS A VACUOUS ONE — IT JUST FAILS IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION. Decoys at 235-343 characters against a 566-character target reported rank 9; rebuilt at comparable length, rank 4. The wrong number was the one that made the problem someone else's, and I reported it before catching it.

A RULING CAN BE ASKED FOR, AGREED, REPORTED AS SETTLED, AND NEVER BUILT. R7 was the answer to my own question and produced no code and no test. Nothing between the ruling and QA's verdict could tell: 153 tests, tsc clean, sync clean, five boundary reports and a handoff checklist were all green. Loading a rule, agreeing with a rule, and applying a rule are three different things.

PER-INSERT TRANSACTIONS ON A FILE-BACKED SQLite FIXTURE ARE 20x SLOWER: 599 inserts is 599 fsyncs, 2999ms against 148ms wrapped. Survivable locally and over vitest's 10s HOOK timeout on CI, where the whole file then reports its tests SKIPPED — which reads like a missing suite rather than a slow one. :memory: fixtures are unaffected, which is why only one file went red.

A BULK EDIT THAT MATCHES `it(` DOES NOT MATCH `it.each([...])(`. Three rows kept vitest's default timeout and passed alone every single time, including in CI where an earlier failure hid them. PER-FILE GREEN IS NOT SUITE GREEN: run the full suite alone before calling a change done, including when the change is 'only tests'.

`git show <ref>:<path>` IS MANGLED BY MSYS IN THE BASH TOOL — it becomes a backslash path and git refuses it. Use PowerShell for ref:path reads. Every amendment and every cross-branch file in this loop was read that way.

THE HOOK RUNS THE BUILD ITS REGISTRATION POINTS AT, and ob_stats is the only honest test of which build is serving a session — the RECONNECT MESSAGE REPORTS SUCCESS EITHER WAY. Note the trap: the recall-trigger census value `hook` is visible from the OLD build too, because that query predates the loop; only the three FIRE COUNTS prove the new one.
